outlook.statement: Company is well positioned to pursue sustainable and profitable growth in FY2027 with strengthened business portfolio, expanded capabilities, broader market presence and stronger foundation for sustainable growth. Long-term outlook for Indian economy and sectors served remains encouraging, supported by favourable consumption trends, increasing formalization and growing demand for innovative and sustainable packaging solutions.

Focus on disciplined execution, strengthening customer relationships, enhancing operational excellence, driving innovation, advancing sustainability and improving productivity. Committed to profitable, resilient and value accretive growth for all stakeholders.

Thriarr Polymers aims to strengthen presence in US market, expand into untapped sectors such as Railways, Defense and Aerospace, and enhance offerings through advanced thermoset and thermoplastic processing supported by global certifications. Planned capacity expansion, continued product innovation and entry into new market segments expected to further strengthen growth trajectory.

Beauty & Personal Care segment: Strengthening position through packaging innovation in body care, travel packs and routine-led formats, developing differentiated solutions aligned with ingredient-led, wellness-driven and premium beauty trends, strengthening partnerships with digital-first brands and online retail platforms.

Bulk Packaging business: Focus on improving capacity utilization to optimize operational efficiencies and profitability, strengthening customer outreach through renewed sales team and targeted business development, enhancing market visibility through industry exhibitions and focused efforts on high-value accounts.

Global economic outlook has turned cautiously guarded; IMF projects global GDP growth at 3.1% in CY 2026 and 3.2% in CY 2027, down from 3.4% in 2025. Downside risks include persistent energy disruptions, inflation, and geopolitical tensions.

India's growth outlook remains strong with real GDP projected at 6.8%-7.2% in FY27, supported by resilient domestic demand, infrastructure spending, and stable macroeconomic fundamentals. Inflation expected to remain within RBI's target band.

Indian rigid plastic packaging industry projected to grow from USD 26.61 billion in 2025 to USD 44.59 billion by 2030 at ~10.9% CAGR. Government targets industry economic activity of USD 126 billion in 4-5 years with 10 approved plastic parks.

Indian FMCG market expected to grow at 17.3% CAGR through 2025-30, reaching nearly USD 643 billion by 2030. Revenue growth of 6-8% expected in FY26 with 4-6% volume increase. Rural markets growing faster than urban for sixth consecutive quarter.

India paints and coatings market expected to grow from USD 11.45 billion in 2025 to USD 12.51 billion in 2026, reaching USD 19.5 billion by 2031 at 9.28% CAGR. Decorative paints comprise ~75% of market.
India agrochemicals market estimated at USD 9 billion in 2025, growing to USD 9.59 billion in 2026. India's food processing industry projected to reach USD 535 billion by end of FY26.

Hitech remains well-positioned to capitalise on emerging opportunities across both domestic and international markets, backed by strong manufacturing capabilities, engineering-led innovation, diversified sectoral presence and a proactive approach towards sustainability and operational excellence.

Focus remained on expanding presence in high-growth sectors such as FMCG and nutraceuticals, while also advancing recyclable PET packaging solutions and lightweight product formats aligned with evolving sustainability requirements.

Significant progress in the commercialisation of In-Mould Labelling (IML) technologies across manufacturing locations. Advanced EBM-based IML solutions integrated with nano-printing technology, enabling anti-counterfeiting and enhanced product authentication capabilities.

Continued evolution of the DSIR-accredited Technology Centre at Pune into a commercially aligned engineering and design platform, supporting simulation-driven product development, rapid prototyping, tooling and customised packaging innovation across multiple sectors.
Initiated development of Dry Powder Inhaler (DPI) and Roto Haler devices during the year, marking entry into precision-oriented healthcare applications.
Further strengthened industrial packaging capabilities through expansion at the Dahej facility, including the addition of new large-format drum SKUs catering to bulk chemical packaging requirements.
Expanded international outreach through Hitech Global Inc. in the United States, supporting stronger customer engagement and future market development initiatives in overseas markets.

Hitech Global Inc. focused on expanding the Company's global footprint by leveraging its design development and technical expertise to penetrate the North American market. A key focus for HGI this year has been the research and development of innovative materials and sustainable alternatives, supporting the Company's commitment to a circular economy.

Thriarr Polymers Private Limited remains dedicated to the manufacturing of high-quality Thermosets and Thermoplastics specifically for electrical switchgear components and assemblies. The integration of TPPL's manufacturing capabilities continues to provide the Company with a robust supply chain and technical synergy in the electrical components segment.
Transitioning the Technology Centre into an independent profitability center over the next 3 to 5 years.
Pilot lot planned for Hitech Own recipe PPCP Compounding in Q2 2026-27.
Expanding global footprint and carefully managing international financial commitments.

Interest rate risk: A fall in the discount rate which is linked to the G.Sec. Rate will increase the present value of the liability requiring higher provision. A fall in the discount rate generally increases the mark to market value of the assets depending on the duration of asset.

Salary Risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan liability is calculated by reference to the future salaries of members. As such, an increase in the salary of the members more than assumed level will increase the plan's liability.

Investment Risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan liability is calculated using a discount rate which is determined by reference to market yields at the end of the reporting period on government bonds. If the return on plan asset is below this rate, it will create a plan deficit.
Supplier finance arrangements may cause concentration of liquidity risk (Ind AS 107 amendment)
Foreign Currency Risk: The Group undertakes transactions denominated in foreign currencies; consequently exposures to exchange rate fluctuations arise.
Credit Risk: Credit risk refers to the risk that a counterparty will default on its contractual obligations resulting in financial loss to the Group.
Interest Rate Risk: Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market interest rates.

Liquidity Risk: Liquidity risk is the risk that the Group will encounter difficulty in raising funds to meet commitments associated with financial instruments that are settled by delivering cash or another financial asset.
Interest rate risk on defined benefit plan: A fall in the discount rate which is linked to the G.Sec. Rate will increase the present value of the liability requiring higher provision.
Asset Liability Matching Risk: The plan faces the ALM risk as to the matching cash flow.
Mortality risk: Since the benefits under the plan is not payable for life time and payable till retirement age only, plan does not have any longevity risk.
Concentration Risk: Plan is having a concentration risk as all the assets are invested with the insurance company and a default will wipe out all the assets.
